verdict.rationale: The GPU is driven programmatically through NVIDIA's documented public CUDA platform. The CUDA Toolkit provides a runtime library, a compiler and accelerated libraries (docs-3), and lets you write kernels in Python (cuTile) or C++ (CUDA Tile) (docs-4, docs-19). Higher-level documented APIs such as RAPIDS/cuML/cuDF (docs-2, docs-34, docs-36) and the Video Codec SDK (docs-39) also target the card. A community critic notes that as an SM120 part it lacks tmem/tcgen05 and is under-supported by the main libraries, which focus on SM100 (comm-6); this narrows the depth of library coverage. missing for 10: RTX PRO 6000-specific API/driver or management documentation (the CUDA docs are generic), hands-on corroboration of programmatic use, and confirmation of full library support for SM120.
